title: Reservoir-based ingress controller and autoscale playbook for embeddings
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:
Customer workloads show highly spiky embedding ingress patterns: short multi-second bursts from search indexing and user-driven rerank requests, followed by long tails of low QPS. Current autoscaler reacts too slowly, queue depth oscillates, and some tenants experience elevated p99 latency or 429s during bursts. We need a deterministic ingress smoothing and autoscaling playbook that reduces p99 tails, keeps throughput predictable, and bounds cost impact for bursty tenants.

Proposal summary:
1) Implement a reservoir-based ingress controller that maintains a small per-tenant reservoir of admission tokens (time-decayed) to absorb short bursts without immediately triggering scale-up. Reservoir replenishment will be tied to recent steady-state throughput and tenant SLA tier.
2) Combine reservoir admission with a predictive target-concurrency estimator (lightweight ML or exponential smoothing) to inform autoscaler fast-path decisions (scale-up when sustained demand exceeds reservoir + headroom for X seconds).
3) Implement a secondary fast-path queue with priority headroom reservation for premium tenants to prevent noisy neighbors from using all burst tokens.
4) Update rate-limiting behavior: for short bursts, prefer enqueue-with-backpressure and informative Retry-After headers; for sustained overage beyond reservoir + grace period, return 429s and emit tenant-level capacity alerts.
5) Deliver a playbook and rollout plan including load tests, canary strategy, and cost sensitivity analysis.

Why this is different from prior work:
- Instead of purely threshold-driven autoscaling or fixed warm pool sizes, the reservoir design smooths short variance while still allowing rapid scale when needed.
- Focus on tenant-level headroom and explicit priority reservation rather than global pool changes.

Success metrics:
- Reduce embedding endpoint p99 latency for bursty tenants by >= 30% under representative burst traces.
- Reduce 429 spike frequency during short bursts by >= 50% for non-malicious traffic patterns.
- Keep 1-month cost delta for autoscaling under +6% for the fleet when enabling reservoirs across staging workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress controller implemented with per-tenant reservoir admission and configurable decay parameters
Predictive target-concurrency estimator integrated with autoscaler and validated on synthetic burst traces
Priority headroom reservation works end-to-end and prevents priority tenants from being evicted during burst absorption
Observability: new metrics emitted (reservoir_tokens, reservoir_replenish_rate, admission_denied, headroom_reserved_by_tenant) and dashboard created
Load tests demonstrating >=30% p99 improvement on example burst traces and 50% reduction in transient 429s
Playbook and runbook documented with rollout steps, rollback criteria, and cost sensitivity analysis
tasks: Design reservoir admission algorithm and select decay parameters (eng + applied-ml)
Implement ingress controller hooks and token store (redis-backed or in-pod ephemeral with sync)
Build predictive concurrency estimator prototype and integration tests
Add priority headroom reservation and configurable tenant tiers
Extend autoscaler to consume reservoir signals and prediction outputs
Create synthetic burst workload generator and benchmark harness
Add metrics and dashboard panels to Console (reservoir-level and fleet-level views)
Run staged load tests (canary in staging -> limited prod rollout)
Write playbook, runbook, and customer-facing notes for behavior change
comments: 2025-02-12 Aisha Patel: Filed initial issue after postmortem showed multiple burst-induced 429s last week. Attached burst traces and affected tenant list.

2025-02-18 Marco Liu: Proposed reservoir design in design doc (see links). Prefers Redis for token persistence to avoid cold-start drift. Wants to keep default decay conservative to avoid over-adsorption.

2025-02-24 Priya Rao (PM): Requested cost estimate and clarification on how headroom tiers are assigned. Suggested we include a config toggle per workspace so sales can enable for premium customers only.
2025-03-01 Dave Nguyen (SRE): Raised concerns about cross-region token consistency for multi-region tenants. Suggests local reservoirs per-region with a smallglobal quota for cross-region bursts.
2025-03-03 Marco Liu: Updated acceptance criteria to include new metrics and dashboard. Starting implementation branch ENG-199342-reservoir-ingress. Planning staging canary next week.
